transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2028-01-19
- Time: 15:00 - 15:57 UTC
- Duration: 57 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Lucas (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Aisha, Mark, Sofia, Diego (Praxis)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood and Praxis reviewed current pilot usage, saw a drop in peak successful requests during holiday traffic; discussed costs per 1k tokens under current hosted configuration vs a Dedicated pilot. Praxis requested a tighter cost model, runbook for failover to dedicated, and the SOC2/ISO packet + network diagram for their security / procurement. Next steps include updated cost tables, SOC/security docs, and a production readiness workshop.

Topics:
- Recent usage trends and attribution of spike to marketing campaign (pages -> generative search)
- Dedicated vs hosted economics and right-sizing options
- Reliability: incident patterns, observed tail latency, KV cache hit rates
- Roadmap & pilot extension: metrics for success and rollout criteria
- Compliance and procurement checklist

Action items (captured in transcript):
- See metadata action_items above

Transcript (timestamps approximate; transcription may include mis-hearings):
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): All right everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick health and velocity sync for Praxis. I think we have about, what, 55 minutes, so we'll run through usage, costs, reliability, then next steps.
[00:18] Aisha (Praxis): Yep sounds good, thanks. We had a medium spike last week when marketing pushed the holiday promo, a couple of requests timed out.
[00:30] Lucas (Redwood): Can you give rough numbers on the spike? QPS or tokens per minute?
[00:38] Mark (Praxis): At peak we saw about 420 rps for a ten minute window, roughly 180k tokens per minute aggregated across features. We also saw elevated tail latency around 1.2s p95 on the hosted route for generation.
[00:55] Lucas: Ok, that aligns with our metrics. I saw the same window — there was a small cold-start effect on some model variants and some prefix cache misses on the product search feature.
[01:07] Diego (Praxis): We observed a handful of 5xx errors. They seemed to correlate with a particular model variant fallback. Is Redwood routing out automatically?
[01:20] Priya (Redwood CSM): Yes, there was a fallback to the lower-tier variant per your routing policy. We can walk through adjusting buffering and prefix caching to reduce p95.
[01:35] Aisha: Quick Q: what's causing those prefix misses? We thought kv cache would catch this pattern.
[01:43] Lucas: Two reasons — one, sequence distribution changed because queries were longer during the campaign (more context tokens), and two, your model sharding had slightly different context windows which reduced shared cache effectiveness. We recommended increasing the KV cache TTL for session-level tokens and enable prefix trimming where safe.
[02:03] Mark: There's also cost impact. When cache miss rate jumps, tokens burned rise and cost per thousand goes up. We need a clear cost table that ties batch size + cache hit rate to unit costs.
[02:17] Lucas: Agreed. We'll produce an updated cost model with scenarios: hosted baseline, hosted with cache tuning, and dedicated pilot numbers including reserved capacity.
[02:29] Sofia (Praxis): From product side we need conversion metrics. If tail latency is above 600ms our conversion drops measurably, so we want to set SLOs around 500-600ms p95 for the critical flows.
[02:44] Priya: Noted — that will go into the pilot success criteria. We'll propose SLOs and a measurement plan including synthetic traffic and canary thresholds.
[02:55] Maya: Let's talk dedicated pilot briefly. Praxis asked about expected throughput per node and failure modes. Lucas, can you run numbers?
[03:03] Lucas: Sure. For the model you're using (open-vic-13b-ish in this pilot), a single dedicated GPU node with optimized kernels and static batching expects sustained 200-300 rps for short completion lengths, assuming 64 token avg. For longer sequences or larger beam width, throughput drops. We'll give node-level numbers and a recommended pool size for your 99th percentile traffic.
[03:28] Aisha: And how does that compare cost-wise? We need to see a 3-month runway projection with commit and without commit.
[03:37] Lucas: We'll show both — reserved capacity (monthly committed) typically reduces unit cost by ~20-35% vs on-demand hosted when utilization is high; but there's the upfront commit tradeoff. We'll build a model that plugs in your forecasted utilization.
[03:53] Diego: On reliability, we need the runbook for failover. In our last incident we had to manually shift traffic. Can Redwood do automatic regional fallback?
[04:03] Maya: Yes, smart routing can failover by policy. However you'll want a canary and a staged rollback plan. We'll supply a runbook draft that includes a checklist for on-call and automated fallover triggers.
[04:18] Mark: Also procurement requires SOC2 docs and a network diagram for our InfoSec.
[04:24] Maya: We'll send our SOC2 and ISO attestations and a sanitized network diagram; Lucas will include the data flow notes for KV cache and where logs are retained.
[04:35] Aisha: About data retention — we need clarity on logs, token retention, and whether you persist any PII.
[04:44] Priya: By default hosted keeps transient request logs for 30 days for debugging and auditing; you can enable longer retention or disable retention for PII-sensitive fields. With Private deployments you can control retention entirely. We'll include options and the KMS/HSM integrations in the security pack.
[05:03] Sofia: For rollout criteria — we want to see stable p95 under 600ms for two weeks and cost within 15% of forecast before broadening new feature release.
[05:15] Maya: OK we'll formalize that as pilot acceptance criteria in the updated doc.
[05:23] Aisha: One more — we noticed model quality drift; some responses were hallucinating product availability. Any guidance to reduce hallucinations?
[05:34] Lucas: We recommend targeted prompt engineering, a reranker for factual retrieval steps, and an optional retrieval augmentation with a freshness TTL. We'll propose a lightweight eval harness to measure hallucination rate per endpoint.
[05:52] Mark: Can you include an eval metric in the cost model so product can see marginal cost per percent decrease in hallucination?
[06:01] Lucas: We'll approximate it — cost of ensembling/reranking vs improvement in false-positive rate.
[06:10] Diego: On-call escalation: who do we reach out to for severity 1 outside business hours?
[06:16] Priya: We'll provide the escalation matrix. For pilots we typically provide a named SE on-call during the initial run and then a rotation agreement if you move to Dedicated.
[06:29] Maya: Quick check — anyone planning to move to Private deployment (VPC) instead of Redwood-hosted?
[06:37] Aisha: Not immediately; procurement wants to see pilot numbers first. But it's on the roadmap for regulated customers in EMEA.
[06:46] Lucas: Ok noted, that affects region routing and audit logging.
[06:52] [Silence / cross-talk for 20s]
[07:14] Lucas: I'll outline three scenarios in the cost spreadsheet: baseline hosted, tuned-hosted (cache + batch change), dedicated pool (reserved + burst config).
[07:24] Maya: And I'll attach the security pack. Priya will coordinate the runbook workshop.
[07:31] Sofia: Is there any benchmarking we can run from our side to simulate peak traffic? We want to validate autoscale and routing under realistic request mixes.
[07:41] Lucas: Yes — we'll share a synthetic load script and a recommended request mix. It will include distribution of sequence lengths and concurrency to mimic your marketing spike.
[07:52] Diego: Is there a way to simulate KV cache warm state for the test? We saw that cold caches cost us.
[07:59] Lucas: We'll provide a pre-warm procedure and a test harness that can replay typical session sequences to approximate a warmed cache.
[08:10] Aisha: Great. On timelines — can we get the security docs by Friday? That's the gating item for procurement.
[08:17] Maya: Yes, we'll get SOC2 and network diagram by 2028-01-21.
[08:23] Mark: And cost model by Tuesday next week?
[08:28] Lucas: I'll have a first pass by 2028-01-24.
[08:33] Sofia: For the workshop — two hours; we'll invite Product, SRE, and Security. Week of 2028-01-30 looks good.
[08:42] Priya: I'll send a calendar invite after we confirm Diego's team's availability.
[08:48] Maya: Anything else on roadmap? We plan to add autoscaling burst nodes and a model-variant that uses low-precision quantization for high throughput — that may reduce cost but could slightly change quality. We can run a small AB test.
[09:07] Aisha: We'll be open to an AB if you can quantify expected quality delta.
[09:13] Lucas: We'll include a quick AB plan with evaluation thresholds.
[09:20] Mark: Final question — if we commit to a Dedicated pool, how long is the provisioning lead time?
[09:26] Maya: Standard lead time is 5-10 business days for reserved capacity depending on region. For urgent needs we can prioritize but it depends on capacity.
[09:36] Diego: Noted.
[09:39] Maya: Ok let's recap and close.
[09:42] Recap (rough):
- Redwood to send SOC2 & network diagram (Maya) by 2028-01-21
- Redwood to deliver cost scenarios spreadsheet (Lucas) by 2028-01-24
- Runbook workshop to be scheduled for week of 2028-01-30 (Priya + Diego)
- SE to share synthetic load script and pre-warm harness (Lucas)
- Define pilot acceptance criteria: p95 < 600ms for 2 weeks and cost within 15% of forecast (Maya/Praxis)

[10:05] Meeting ends.

Notes: transcript imperfect — some numeric values may be slightly off from system logs. References: shared deck (redwood/praxis-prod-readout-2028-01-19.pptx), cost spreadsheet link (drive/praxis-pilot-costs), SOC packet (link provided in follow-up).
